title: feat(plugin-approvals): opening an approval step tells each resolved approver (approval.requested)
body:
Fixes #22607
Clause-②: yes

Opening an approval step now tells the people it landed on. `openNodeRequest` publishes the new topic `approval.requested` to each concrete approver on the slate the request opened on. It goes through `notify()`, the same single ingress (ADR-0030) and payload shape that `approval.reminder` and every other sibling topic use. There is no second notification path. The approvals guide's callout "Opening a request notifies nobody" is rewritten. Its `manager_id` sentences now name the Console surface that writes the column: Setup → Users → ⋯ → Set Manager.

Dispatched by the `domain:services` seat 1 PM, session `session_013j5gkUCpqQiti4GgPqqmnt`. Claim `6094034487`, triage `6093976698`.

## Measured first: who followed the guide's workaround

The guide used to recommend "a `notify` node next to the approval node" as the way to tell approvers. A flow that did that would now tell the same approvers twice. I counted every flow that holds an approval node, and classified each `notify` node in it by edge reachability: reachable from an approval node means it runs after the decision (outcome messaging, not the workaround), otherwise it runs before or beside the approval node (a workaround candidate).

| tree (commit) | flows with an approval node | approval nodes | `notify` nodes in those flows | before or beside the approval (workaround) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| this repo `examples/` (`d748ae80af`; 31 flows scanned) | 8 | 15 | 1 (`showcase_invoice_signoff.notify_cleared`, after the decision) | **0** |
| `objectstack-ai/hotcrm` `src/` (`f0afcbd`) | 5 | 6 | 6 (all `notify_approved` / `notify_rejected`) | **0** |
| `objectstack-ai/hotclm` `src/` (`46e65f0`, and PR #101's head `0089ffa`) | 1 | 6 | 2 (`notify_approved` / `notify_rejected`) | **0** |

Control on the parser: hotcrm's grep for approval nodes returns 11 hits = 5 doc-comment mentions + the 6 real nodes the parser found. I also searched all three trees for a flow or hook triggered by `sys_approval_request` creation that notifies approvers. None exists. No measured app double-notifies. The changeset still names the remedy for apps outside these trees.

## Where the topic is declared

Measured: nowhere but the call site. The sibling topics are string literals at their `notify()` call sites in `approval-service.ts`. `service-messaging` keeps no topic catalog: a topic is a free string, keyed only by the preference filter, and `mandatoryTopics` defaults to empty. `packages/spec` declares none of them. So this PR adds no spec change and no registry row.

The name is `approval.requested`. The card asks for "an `approval.requested`-style topic", ADR-0012's Layer-1 event example names `approval.requested`, and the sibling vocabulary uses past participles (`reassigned`, `escalated`, `returned`, `ooo_substituted`).

## The recipient rule, and how it matches the reminder's

`remind()` fans out over the slate's concrete identities (a user id or an email), sending one `notify()` per approver. A `type:value` literal gets no personal message: `notify()` drops every slot address from every audience, so the reminder's literal arm reaches nobody. The opening applies the same rule to the slate it actually opened on, which is after OOO delegation and after an `onEmptyApprovers: 'fallback'` replacement:

- each concrete approver gets one emit with `audience: [approver]`, `source` = the request, `actionUrl` deep-linked to it by `notify()`, and the opening run's person as the actor;
- each person is told **once**: per-group tagging can list one person twice on the slate, and the fan-out de-duplicates;
- a literal slot (`position:NAME` with no holders) gets no message. So a slate of literals only notifies nobody, and `onEmptyApprovers` decides that case: `admin_rescue` opens and tells nobody, `auto_approve` and `fail` open nothing, `fallback` opens on and tells the fallback approvers;
- an out-of-office **delegate** gets exactly one message, the existing `approval.ooo_substituted`, not a second one for the opening.

The send happens last, after every write of the opening has landed. Like every `notify()`, it is best-effort: a channel that throws logs a warning and never fails the opening.

**Deliberately not included:** one-tap Approve / Reject links. ADR-0043 mints those bearer tokens in `remind()` only, and minting them on every opening is a decision this card does not make.

## Pins (`approval-requested-notification.integration.test.ts`)

These run on the real `ApprovalService`, on a real `ObjectQL` over `SqlDriver` (in-memory better-sqlite3, real DDL). No new fake engine.

1. Opening a step puts one message in each resolved approver's inbox: a named user plus both holders of a staffed position get exactly three emits, one per person, with the reminder's payload shape, source, deep link and actor.
2. A person the slate lists under two groups is told once.
3. A mixed slate (unstaffed position plus a user) tells only the user.
4. Control: a step whose approvers resolve to nobody notifies no one, and `onEmptyApprovers` decides it. Four cases: `admin_rescue` (opens, tells nobody), `auto_approve` (no request, no emit), `fail` (refused, no emit), `fallback` (opens on and tells the fallback approver).
5. An OOO delegate is told once, by `approval.ooo_substituted`.
6. A channel that throws never fails the opening, and the failure is logged with the topic.

Existing batteries widened to the new call site: `approval-notification-body.integration.test.ts` (the site census is now twelve of thirteen call sites, and every new emit carries a non-empty `body` and no undeclared payload field) and `actor-lookups-hold-ids.integration.test.ts` (the opening forwards the person, never the email slot). Four tests in `approval-service.test.ts` attached messaging before opening and then read `emitted[0]` or the total count as if their own step were the only sender. Each now asserts that the opening sent exactly `approval.requested`, clears the array, and keeps its original assertions unchanged.

### Ablation: the publish removed

`node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` replaced `for (const approver of openedOn) {` with `for (const approver of [] as string[]) {` (anchor hits 1 → 0, blob `2a30646be68a` → `8e67159c79bf`). It ran at committed HEAD `36f03883d3`, which holds the implementation and every pin, with a trap-armed restore. The subject is imported relatively from `src/`, so no `dist/` is involved.

- **Mutated:** 12 failed / 359 passed across the 4 files. Red: all six positive pins in the new file, both widened batteries, and the four scoped tests. **Green, as expected:** the three empty-slate controls (`admin_rescue`, `auto_approve`, `fail`).
- **Restored:** blob back to `2a30646be68a` = HEAD's blob, `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status` clean.

## Docs (`content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`)

- The callout "Opening a request notifies nobody" (`:451`) is rewritten to describe the new topic: who is told, who is not and why, and the remedy for a flow with a `notify` node beside its approval node.
- `:380`: "`sys_user.manager_id`, which no product surface writes" now names **Setup → Users → ⋯ → Set Manager**. Verified on `main`: `sys_user`'s row action `set_user_manager` ("Set Manager", list row menu and record header, platform admins only, hidden for `idp_provisioned` identities) posts to `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/set-user-manager`.
- Bounded in-place fix, same defect: `:32` carried the identical false sentence ("resolves from a column no product surface writes") and now names the same surface. The `manager` callout's "A platform admin posts the link" now leads with the same Console action before the endpoint. All four in-place conditions hold: same defect class as item 2, a mechanical rewrite in the form item 2 fixes, no other claim on the file (#22584, which covers `:384`–`:386` of this page, is an unclaimed `pm:queue` issue), and the same gate family. #22584's sentence itself is untouched.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run --project repo` (spec `test:repo`, which scans `content/docs`) :: exit 0, **54 files / 915 tests passed**.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` :: exit 0, "All 15 generated artifacts are up to date".
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived **96** gate commands from this diff. All 96 ran on this HEAD, each **exit 0**. `--ran` reconciliation: "96 derived, 96 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN", a derived zero because every line carries its exit code. On the pre-merge HEAD, `check:skill-examples`, `check:i18n` and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first answered exit 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET, missing `dist/`). After their named prerequisite builds they measured green, and the post-merge sweep ran them green.
- Ablation: see above (12 red / 359 green while mutated, restore proven).
- Not run locally: the `integration`-tier and dogfood suites of other packages, and the repo-wide lint. Those runs belong to CI. Out-of-package readers of approver inboxes were checked by reading them (Acceptance notes).

## Acceptance notes

- **ADR-0043 says the opposite in one parenthetical.** `docs/adr/0043-actionable-approval-links.md` `:40`–`:42` (Accepted) says "(Open-time notification remains the flow author's `notify` node; templates there can adopt the same links later.)" After this PR that sentence is stale. I read it as a v1 scope note, not a recorded decision: it sits in Mechanics, weighs no alternative, gives no rationale, and anticipates a "later". ADR-0030's single-ingress decision also names "approval requests" as a producer. Amending ADR-0043 is a Tier H edit and is not in this PR. It is raised as an open question in the dev report.
- `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/approvals.json` `:341`, `:394` and `:400` state that "opening a request notifies NOBODY" and that "no approval.opened topic exists". After this PR those notes are stale but harmless: the fixtures they describe still drive `remind` / `reassign`. The file is outside this claim's surface; owner: none.
- No end-to-end inbox pin in `packages/qa/dogfood` (outside this claim's surface). The new emit uses the reminder's channel, whose delivery to `sys_inbox_message` the card measured on 17.7.0 (`remind` → the Executive's inbox `total 1`).
- `examples/app-showcase/src/automation/flows/index.ts:1262` says the dual sign-off's approvers "are notified concurrently". That is now true for staffed holders, so no change.
- Existing readers of approver inboxes outside this package all filter by topic or title (`approval-notification-body.dogfood.test.ts`, `seed-ownership-claim-dispatch.dogfood.test.ts`, `examples/app-showcase/test/approval-resume-relation-expand.test.ts`). None counts all of an approver's messages.
